title: UTF-8 and UTF-16
description:
Convert between UTF-8 and UTF-16, the job of `MultiByteToWideChar` and `WideCharToMultiByte`.

```
"héllo" UTF-8 (6 bytes) -> UTF-16 (5 units)
"😀" UTF-8 F0 9F 98 80 -> UTF-16 D83D DE00 (a surrogate pair)
bad UTF-8 C3 28 -> refused at byte 0
```
hints: A lead byte `110xxxxx` starts 2 bytes, `1110xxxx` 3 and `11110xxx` 4; each follower must be `10xxxxxx` (lesson 1.02).
A code point `cp` above 0xFFFF: `cp -= 0x10000; high = 0xD800 + (cp >> 10); low = 0xDC00 + (cp & 0x3FF);`.
`std::u16string` is the standard string of `char16_t`, 16-bit code units: what `std::wstring` is on Windows, but 16 bits on every compiler. It works like `std::string`, and `u"..."` makes a literal.
requirements: Decode 1 to 4 byte sequences and refuse invalid ones; code points above 0xFFFF become surrogate pairs.
Round-trip a few strings and check they come back the same.
stretch: Refuse "overlong" encodings like `C0 AF` for `/`: a sequence is overlong when its value would fit in fewer bytes (a 2-byte sequence below 0x80, a 3-byte one below 0x800, a 4-byte one below 0x10000).
